milestone: M4 — voice reliability, private calls, screen sharing, relay paths

architecture_decision.choice: extend the embedded Pion SFU and rewrite its publication model
architecture_decision.basis: the authorization/privacy/resume/TURN control plane is already built and tested in-process; an external SFU would re-implement all of it across a network boundary, and the one-binary deployment is most of what makes the product approachable
architecture_decision.conditional_on: a video-forwarding measurement at the reference allocation; the plan puts two 2.5 Mbit/s shares to nine viewers at roughly 45 Mbit/s of egress from a process also serving HTTP, SQLite and WebSocket

delivered.TURN TCP fallback: the relay offers UDP and TCP on one ICE server; a test drives a real STUN Binding Request over the TCP listener and checks the echoed transaction id
delivered.TURN advertised host: configurable, so a relay behind NAT does not advertise its listening address
delivered.publication model: a publication is an object with a stable id, owner, kind and lifecycle; screen video is H.264 at 90 kHz and audio is Opus at 48 kHz and the two are never written through the same forwarder
delivered.renegotiation: a second offer naming a screen is accepted, bounded, and gated on the same voice.speak decision as the microphone

not_delivered_yet: The screen track is negotiated but not yet forwarded: the SFU still forwards audio by slot and no client calls getDisplayMedia.
Private calls: admission still resolves a db.Channel and refuses anything whose Type != voice, so a direct or group conversation cannot host a call.
The 24-hour race suite has not been run for this schema.
No physical microphone, capture, or restricted-network observation exists.

rehearsals.note: the recovery and browser figures were recorded at schema 20 and before the publication model; the rtc and api suites are current
